message.text:
These are concurrency-limiting semaphores (bounding parallel work), not per-user request-rate limiting. No such middleware exists.

r02.

**Premise correction**: There is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware anywhere in this codebase — I found no rate-limiting library in `go.mod`/`go.sum` (no `golang.org/x/time/rate`, no third-party limiter package), no registration of any such middleware in the Echo server setup, and no custom implementation under `server/` or `internal/`.

What actually exists is unrelated to rate limiting:
- The only middleware registered on the HTTP server (`server/server.go:51-52`) is `middleware.Recover()` (panic recovery) and a custom CORS middleware (`newCORSMiddleware`) — neither limits request rate.
- There are two `golang.org/x/sync/semaphore.Weighted` instances — `thumbnailSemaphore` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:40,59` and `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107,116`) and `imageProcessingSemaphore` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:41,60`) — but these only bound *concurrency* (max simultaneous thumbnail/image-processing jobs per process), not the *rate* of requests a given user can make, and they aren't scoped per-user.
- A doc comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86` merely advises "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse" as a security recommendation for operators — it is not an implementation.

So there is nothing to cite as "the per-user API rate-limiting middleware" or its limits, because that feature does not exist in this repository.
